channel.title: The Australian Mining Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Australian Mining Review (australianminingreview.com.au)

item.title: Japan and South Korea accelerate nuclear growth
item.description: The Middle East conflict is reinforcing energy security as a central pillar of power planning in Japan and South Korea.

item.title: Deep sea mining talks deadlocked
item.description: International Seabed Authority (ISA) Council negotiations have concluded without the adoption of an agreed upon mining code and without any mining approvals being granted.

item.title: MCA pushes for $13m AI trial proposal
item.description: The Minerals Council of Australia (MCA) has asked the Federal Government to fund a three-year pilot program to embed AI into environmental regulatory decision-making.

item.title: Billion-dollar copper project to deliver local benefits
item.description: The post Billion-dollar copper project to deliver local benefits appeared first on The Australian Mining Review.

item.title: Liberty Bell Bay smelter enters voluntary administration
item.description: Liberty Bell Bay in Tasmania, one of billionaire Sanjeev Gupta’s last remaining Australian assets, has entered voluntary administration.

item.title: Sandvik awarded major order from Byrnecut
item.description: Sandvik has received five AutoMine orders from Byrnecut, the world’s largest underground mining contractor, for operations across Australia and Namibia.

item.title: Rio’s iron ore production resilient despite cyclone
item.description: Rio Tinto (ASX: RIO) has reported its iron ore port operations have resumed after Tropical Cyclone Narelle passed over WA’s Pilbara region.

item.title: Albanese cuts fuel excise in half
item.description: The Federal Government is halving fuel excise costs by more than $.26/L for three months to deliver immediate fuel relief to households and industry.

item.title: Energy market shock expected to drive inflation
item.description: Australia’s economic outlook has shifted following escalation of conflict in the Middle East as rising energy costs are expected to push inflation higher than previously forecast, according to Commonwealth Bank economists.

item.title: WA resources sector award nominations now open
item.description: The WA Government has opened nominations for the 2026 Resource Sector Awards for Excellence.

item.title: Rio backs Lifeline WA with $1.8m boost
item.description: Lifeline WA and Rio Tinto (ASX: RIO) have entered a new four year partnership to support the hundreds of Western Australian volunteers who answer calls from people in crisis.

item.title: Mining drives doubling electricity demand in South Australia
item.description: South Australia is on the verge of a ‘once-in-a-generation’ economic growth opportunity, underpinned by affordable, reliable and sustainable electricity, according to a report by ElectraNet.

item.title: Liebherr’s proven performance in the Pilbara
item.description: Liebherr’s T 264 mining trucks are proving their reliability in one of WA’s most demanding environments, with a fleet now working at a Thiess-operated site in the Pilbara.

item.title: UQ ranked top five globally for mining engineering
item.description: The University of Queensland (UQ) has been ranked 5th in the world in the 2026 QS World University Rankings by Subject for mineral and mining engineering.

item.title: Sugarbag Hill declared prescribed project
item.description: The Queensland Government has declared the Sugarbag Hill project in north Queensland a prescribed project to fast-track delivery.
